args.query: expired certificate mTLS bank partner payment failures
error rate dashboard green but payments failing PENDING_RETRY

events.statement: payment-service ERROR logs from 12:15:27Z onward show mTLS handshake rejections to bank-partner-api and an expired client certificate.
The two dominant ERROR patterns (171 cert-expiry + 140 PENDING_RETRY) account for 311 of 313 WARN/ERROR entries; failures persist through the latest data at 13:58:39Z.
The expired client cert's notAfter is exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; failures begin immediately after (12:15:27Z first PENDING_RETRY).
payment-service HTTP error_rate metric stays flat (~0.18-0.32%) across the whole window, explaining the green dashboard.
bank_api_error_rate jumps from ~0.2% to 100% starting in the 12:10-12:20 bucket and stays at 100% through 13:50.
payment_success_rate collapses from ~99% to ~2.5% at the same onset, corroborating real customer-facing payment failures.
Resource/health metrics are normal and stable: request_rate ~100 req/s, cpu_pct ~30%, memory_pct ~55%, db_pool_in_use ~8, restarts 0 throughout.
Only one config change near onset: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z, ~55 min BEFORE the failure onset.
Only deployment in scope is settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z (new CSV exporter); no payment-service deploy and no settlement-service config change.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no telemetry; payment-service is its only caller and observes it via its own logs.
The failure is a client-side certificate expiry: the alert is raised against OUR client cert named payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, not a server/partner-side cert.
payments are marked PENDING_RETRY rather than surfaced as HTTP 5xx, which is why the HTTP error_rate panel (5xx-based) stayed green while actual payment success dropped.
Historical incident HIST-106 is the same class of fault: a settlement-service client certificate expiry without renewal automation, resolved by issuing a new cert and adding an expiry alert.
